bib.title: Synthetic Computers at Scale for Long-Horizon Productivity Simulation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Synthetic Computers at Scale for Long-Horizon Productivity Simulation", Tao Ge (first), Baolin Peng, Hao Cheng, Jianfeng Gao (Microsoft). Technical report, arXiv:2604.28181v1 [cs.AI], 30 Apr 2026. Not peer reviewed ("preprint"). Dataset: huggingface.co/datasets/microsoft/synthetic-computers-at-scale.
COVERAGE: 33 of 33 pages read (121,670 chars), including Appendix A (pp.25-33). References skimmed. The extraction was clean.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Notes 06/05. Occupation skills distilled from simulation retrospectives improve the agent on 100 held-out synthetic computers: 61.6% to 68.6%, +7.0 pp, winning 83/100 paired.
 setup: Claude Code SDK with Sonnet 4.6 as work agent. 900 train / 100 test computers. No weights updated (fn 5). Rubric judge is Opus 4.6. Single run per arm is implied; no seeds or CIs are reported.
 quote: "Baseline 61.6% ... Skill-augmented 68.6% ... ∆ +7.0 pp ... Skill-augmented better 83 (83%) Baseline better 17 (17%)" p.18
2. Notes 06. Scaling in the number of simulated computers (ablation): 10 computers gives no gain, and more computers gives monotonic gains.
 setup: same 100 test computers, paired win/lose.
 quote: "Skills extracted from 100, 500, and 900 computers win on 64%, 75%, and 83% of the test computers" p.19. Fig 7: N=10 is 50/50, with 48/52 shown in the figure. The authors say N=10 "does not improve over the baseline" because occupation coverage is too thin and a mismatched skill "can even hurt".
3. Notes 05/06. Out-of-domain transfer to GDPVal (220 tasks, official rubrics). Pairwise judging by an Opus 4.6 judge against the baseline.
 Fig 8 (win/tie/loss):
 - Sonnet 4.6: 105/48/67, one-sided p=0.002, two-sided p=0.005.
 - Haiku 4.5: 104/36/80, p1=0.045, p2=0.090 (not significant two-sided).
 - Opus 4.6: 99/50/71, p1=0.019, p2=0.038.
 The skills come from Sonnet trajectories, so Haiku and Opus are cross-model transfer. The authors call the gains "weaker".
 quote: "the skill-augmented agent wins 105 tasks and loses 67, with significant one-sided and two-sided sign tests (p= 0.002 and p= 0.005)" p.19
4. Notes 06. Scale and cost of the environment pipeline: 1,000 personas become 1,000 synthetic computers. Pipeline: persona to user profile to filesystem policy to file plan with dependency graph to artifacts created in Kahn topological order. Each simulation is about a month of work, 20 working days, 5 deliverables, run as weekly planning plus one agent session per day.
 number: 2,272 turns and 8.59 h on average (max 3,248 turns, 11.67 h). 5.5 collaborators, 31 communications. Files go from 111.6 to 197.4 per computer. DOCX/XLSX/PDF/PPTX are 67.8% of files.
 quote: "On average, the work agent takes 2,272 turns and 8.59 hours to complete one simulation" p.14
 Compare with GDPVal: 31 turns and 17 min (Table 5, p.19).
5. Notes 06/07. Baseline agent quality on the rubric: most scores are 60-80%. Rubrics are built from 5 repeat runs of the same setting, merged by an Opus judge. The rubric mixes spec, interaction, expertise, reference and quality items (the sample has 55 items and 176 points). Applied to 100 sampled computers. This is rubric-as-reward design, but it is used only for evaluation and not for RL.
 quote: "Most scores fall between 60% and 80%" p.16
6. Notes 05/06 (the failure-mode data). Appendix A, a retrospective for one run (Margaret Forsythe, financial advisor): 605/846 = 71.5%. Deliverable scores range from 54.8% (ESG) to 88.2% (Castellano). Failure modes:
 - cross-document inconsistency, costing about 80-100 points;
 - uncorrected collaborator-flagged errors, about 40 points;
 - 10 blank messages to collaborators in Days 14-20, read by the authors as running low on context;
 - missing components;
 - page-count shortfall: 11 pages against a spec of 18-22.
 quote: "systemic cross-document consistency failure that affected every single deliverable" p.25
 These retrospectives are the "process signal" that feeds the skills (p.17).

LIMITS
- No RL or weight training was done. The paper proposes agentic RL and distillation into weights as future work (Fig 9, Sec 5.1), and it states "we do not update model weights" (p.17 fn5). The claim "substrate for agentic RL" is an argument, not a result.
- All models are Anthropic (Sonnet 4.6 agent, Opus 4.6 setup and judge, Haiku/Opus transfer). The judge and the generator are from the same family, and the Opus judge scores Sonnet work. No human validation of the judge is reported. No seeds, confidence intervals or repeats are given for Table 4. GDPVal uses sign tests.
- The 1,000-computer scale is "preliminary". "Millions or billions" is extrapolation.
- The authors concede (p.22) that artifacts have uniform style, filesystems are too clean, and collaborators are mostly reactive. Some planned web downloads fall back to synthesis (fn 2, p.7).
- Skills sets that grow may become "too large to carry as external instructions" (p.20).
- Only the 100 computers (50 Windows, 50 macOS) plus 500 retrospective reports are released. The 1,000 simulations and trajectories are not.
- The test computers share a persona distribution with the training computers (in-domain), and there is no ablation against generic non-occupation skills or against a random-skill baseline.
- The stated rubric design is described as "simple" (fn 4).

BUILDS ON: Ge et al. 2024 (Persona Hub, persona-driven synthetic data, 370M elite personas); GDPVal (Patwardhan et al., 2025); Kahn 1962 (topological order); Anthropic skill-creator and skills; MiniMax Office skills; AutoForge (Cai et al., 2025, environment synthesis for agentic RL); and Xia et al. 2026, Lu et al. 2026 and Cai et al. 2026 for skill-based improvement.

CODE: none.

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p.1) and Fig 2 (p.3), the pipeline overview. Fig 7 (p.18), the win rate versus number of training computers. Fig 8 (p.19), the GDPVal win/tie/loss for three models. Fig 9 (p.20), the self-improvement loop: simulate, extract skills, distill into weights, reset skills.

QUOTES for the notes (verbatim)
- "each run requires over 8 hours of agent runtime and spans more than 2,000 turns on average" (p.1)
- "we do not update model weights in this evaluation" (p.17 fn5)
- "Synthetic data must synthesize the context, not only the task." (p.2)

PROBLEMS: none. The text contains no embedded instructions. Figure-level checks were not run, since the numbers come from text. Fig 7 and Fig 8 values were read from extracted figure text.
